current_binding_checks.note: Source completeness was independently judged from the two actual original images, not inferred from author inventory or native PASS.

original_opening.observations: Single filled rectangular support/common suspension vertex; two oblique strings and two filled balls on one horizontal line; solid center vertical extending below that line. One left-string l, two top alpha marks and one lower-right alpha mark; the right auxiliary vertical joins string and ball baseline. Two upward/inward tension arrowheads, two outward horizontal arrowheads and two downward weight arrowheads. One left-half r/2 dimension below the balls with two opposing dimension heads. No charge signs, A/B/C, numerical lengths, angles or force values.

comparison: Common pivot, equal-string symmetric layout, ball-center baseline, extended center reference, all three angle marks/arcs, auxiliary outline and single left-half stacked r/2 dimension are retained. No full-r or right-half dimension was invented.

All six force arrows start at the correct ball: tensions follow their strings toward the pivot, horizontal repulsion points outward, and weights point down. The two dimension heads remain distinct from force heads.

Right-side force labels retain their assignments. English elastic localizes the canonical tension subscript; G identifies gravity from current /prose/18 (p0159#9). Small original suffix/lower-edge force lettering remains uncertain: this is explicit current-text notation, not a claim to reconstruct ambiguous source ink.

Coordinates, enlarged angle opening, arrow spans and responsive aspect ratio are unmeasured schematic regularization. They do not claim the worked example's numerical angle, force scale, extra mass or charge values.

The direction assignments match the frozen example context at /prose/24..41: first charge negative, middle/right positive; first pair of forces rightward, second pair leftward, third opposing. No additional resultant or solved numerical annotation was introduced.

Original and modern arrow lengths are uncalibrated. Relative group spacing is not the source's 0.4m/0.6m separation; the spec explicitly disclaims distance and force-ratio scales. The right pair does not assert exact equality, and current text's greater leftward force is not contradicted.
A/B/C are absent in these originals and were not invented. No source cultural lettering or unsupported particle identity was introduced.
